messages:
anya: Noticing a repeat of last month's latency cluster during the 02:00 UTC hour. p99 for /v1/chat up ~3x baseline. Pattern looks similar to previous KV-cache churn incidents.

zhou: Can you share the metric slice? region/instance?

anya: US-east mainly, lp-*-gpu instances. p95 from 120ms->340ms, p99 from 420ms->1.3s for ~12m. No traffic surge.

kevin: I pulled traces: lots of KV miss storms coupled with long prompt tails. Also saw higher queue length on one GPU shard.

tara: Sounds like recurring mode. We should treat this as a pattern, not a one-off. Proposing: a) create a recurring postmortem action to harden cache defaults, b) add an SLO tier for 'long-prompt' workloads with separate p99, c) auto-pause risky canaries that touch KV. Thoughts?

anya: I like (c). For (b) we can surface a separate p99 metric for requests >800 tokens. That will help segment.

zhou: For (a) I can put a config guard that prevents TTL=0 rolling into any canary >5% traffic. Owner: zhou, due: 2024-06-01.

kevin: I'll add a dashboard heatmap showing p99 by token-bucket and backend shard. Owner: kevin, due: 48h.

tara: I'll draft an SLO proposal: keep global p95/p99 as-is, but add an operational SLO for long-prompt p99 with a 1.2s target and its own error budget. Also add a policy: any KV-related config change requires a canary + 24h gated observation before promotion. Owner: tara, due: 2024-06-03.

anya: Also request an automated detector: if p99 for long-prompt cohort >2x baseline for 10m, trigger a high-priority alert and auto-scale backup pool. Owner: anya, due: 2024-05-15.

zhou: I'll implement the canary guard and add a canary tag so we can query TTL variants.

kevin: Dashboard panels + runbook snippet incoming. Runbook steps: check long-prompt p99, KV miss ratio, GPU queue length, canary tag correlation.

tara: Governance note: we'll propose the long-prompt SLO at next SLO sync. If accepted, we need a short public note to sales/support about the new error-budget semantics.

anya: Creating a follow-up ticket with checklist: config guard PR, canary tag, dashboard heatmap, SLO draft, detector, runbook. Assigning owners per thread.

sre-bot: Incident 2024-05-10-0200: follow-up created. Owners: zhou, kevin, tara, anya.

anya: We'll review status in Friday's SLO sync and next oncall handoff. Keep updates brief here.
